title: Waqf and ibtida': four types of stop: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y8 lesson 5 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Waqf and ibtida' rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 5. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Why stopping matters
points: A poor stop can change the meaning

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
a bad stop that spoils the meaning

questions.q: Is stopping at the end of 70:7 «وَنَرَىٰهُ قَرِيبًۭا» tamm, kafi or hasan? Explain.
questions.a: Kafi: the meaning is complete, but 70:8 continues the same idea (the Day).

questions.q: Stop map (pupil PDF): label the stop at the end of each ayah of 70:1 to 11 as tamm, kafi or hasan. Today's rota group recites 70:1 to 11.
questions.a: Most ends are kafi or hasan because 70:1 to 4 and 70:8 to 11 are linked sentences; the end of 70:7 is kafi.

questions.q: Extend: find the waqf sign in 70:11 and say what it allows.
questions.a: ۚ after يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ: stopping and continuing are both allowed.

questions.q: Stretch: why do we still say stopping at every ayah end is sunnah, even when the meaning continues?
questions.a: The Prophet ﷺ is reported to have paused at the end of each ayah when reciting.

questions.q: A stop that breaks or changes the meaning is ...
questions.a: A) qabih (bad). Qabih: a bad stop; go back and restart.

questions.q: After a qabih stop you should ...
questions.a: go back to a good start
options: go back to a good start
carry on from the next word

questions.q: Think again: Read 'Do not approach prayer' and stop. Now read on: 'while you are intoxicated' (4:43). What did the first stop do?
questions.a: Stopping early made it sound like a ban on prayer; the full ayah is about not praying while intoxicated.
